title: Measurement Source
description: Trust-source disambiguator for a vendor-defined metric — *who* produced the number relative to the seller reporting it, not *how* it was produced. Methodology (instrument, model, panel, sensor) is an open corpus and lives at the vendor's measurement-agent catalog (`get_adcp_capabilities.measurement.metrics[]`: `description`, `methodology_url`, `methodology_version`, `standard_reference`, `accreditations[]`); this enum is the one closed axis a buyer agent needs to branch on. The relationship is a property of the (seller, vendor) pair, not of the vendor: the same measurement agent is `first_party` when its operator sells the inventory and `third_party` when an unrelated seller reports the same metric. Declared by the seller on `reporting_capabilities.vendor_metrics[]` and MAY be echoed on `vendor_metric_values[]` rows so a delivery report is self-describing without a discovery hop. Generalises the `completion_source` pattern (`seller_attested` / `vendor_attested`) from `completion_rate` to every vendor metric. The trust axis is independence from the seller's revenue interest — not who runs the SDK, sensor, or model.

enumDescriptions.first_party: The seller (or the seller's own measurement agent) produced the number. Covers seller-operated sensors (DOOH camera or WiFi presence, in-store retail-media counting, cinema audience counting), walled-garden self-reported measurement, and any case where `vendor` resolves to the selling party's own `brand.json`. The seller MUST still publish the metric in a `brand.json` `agents[type='measurement']` catalog like any other vendor; `first_party` is a disclosure, not an exemption from the catalog contract.
enumDescriptions.affiliated: The vendor is a distinct legal entity that shares ownership, a parent, or a material commercial dependency with the seller — a measurement subsidiary, a joint venture, or a vendor whose principal customer is the seller. Not independent enough to be `third_party`; not the seller itself. Buyers MAY treat `affiliated` as `first_party` for trust-discount purposes.
enumDescriptions.third_party: An independent measurement vendor with no ownership or affiliate relationship to the seller (Nielsen, DoubleVerify, IAS, Adelaide, Lumen, TVision, Scope3, Kantar, etc.). Source of truth is the vendor. This is the topology the `vendor_metric` surface was designed around and the value buyers SHOULD assume when a third-party vendor's `brand.json` is clearly unrelated to the seller and the seller omits the field.
